Items.Question: Why do you think people travel more nowadays compared to the past?
Items.ModelAnswer: There are several factors. First, transportation has become much more affordable and accessible. Budget airlines and high-speed trains make it easy for ordinary people to explore. Second, social media fuels wanderlust — seeing photos of exotic destinations inspires people to book trips. Third, rising disposable income in developing countries means more families can afford holidays. It's a combination of technology, economics, and psychology.

Items.Vocabulary: affordable (giá cả phải chăng), accessible (dễ tiếp cận), wanderlust (khao khát đi lại), disposable income (thu nhập khả dụng), exotic destinations (địa điểm kỳ lạ)
Items.Tips: Part 3 cần lập luận có cấu trúc: First/Second/Third. Dùng từ nối: combination of. Phát âm rõ 'wanderlust', 'disposable income'.

Items.Question: Do you think technology has changed the way people communicate?
Items.ModelAnswer: Absolutely. Technology has revolutionized communication. We've shifted from face-to-face and landlines to instant messaging, video calls, and social platforms. This brings convenience — we can stay connected across time zones instantly. However, it also reduces depth. Text-based communication lacks tone and nuance, leading to misunderstandings. People also feel pressured to be always available, which causes burnout. So it's a double-edged sword.

Items.Question: What are the advantages and disadvantages of working from home?
Items.ModelAnswer: Working from home offers flexibility — you can manage your schedule around personal commitments. There's no commute, saving time and money. You can create a personalized workspace. On the flip side, isolation is a real issue. You miss spontaneous collaboration and social interaction. Work-life boundaries blur, leading to longer hours. Not everyone has a suitable home environment. Hybrid models seem to capture the best of both worlds.
